why: Plan section 3, callbacks that throw. A throwing callee inside an array callback ends the loop at the first throwing element, the loop's partial state kept, and the fault takes the statement's route; inside a then handler it rejects the promise the link returns. check is untouched. scaled maps a negative element to zero instead of throwing (unproved; lane B WITNESS on an array holding a negative). total moves a pure value after the forEach loop (proved: the loop helper is the same, the fault exit unchanged). later resolves a negative value instead of rejecting (unproved; WITNESS). ordered moves a pure value after the throwing call inside the handler (proved). guarded drops a check the second one implies (proved: the handler leaves at the first fault, so both reject on the same values with the same error). times is untouched; viaCall calls a throwing unit with its receiver through call, the candidate through apply with an array literal (proved: the same call, its fault routed as a direct call's). callOne swallows the throw of a unit called through call (unproved; WITNESS); callOrdered moves a pure value after such a call (proved). both: the parent throws when a is negative, the candidate checks 0 in its place (must not prove; WITNESS): a loop that ran on after a fault, the next call clearing it, would read both sides alike. A call of a stored throwing function value stays refused: fixtures/escapes/ts/exception_callback_call_stored.ts. A callback handed to an outside function whose body throws stays refused: fixtures/escapes/ts/exception_callback_outside.ts. middle: the parent throws at the second element when b is negative, the candidate checks 0 there (must not prove; WITNESS).
